name: The Ritz London
positioning: Historic Piccadilly hotel opened in 1906 by Cesar Ritz, set between Piccadilly and Green Park, known for its Afternoon Tea, The Ritz Restaurant and The Rivoli Bar
best_for: Travelers who want a classic Afternoon Tea and formal dining under one roof
Families, with a dedicated children's package and a Children's Afternoon Tea

facts.text: The Ritz opened in 1906 and was conceived by the hotelier Cesar Ritz.
The hotel sits between Piccadilly and Green Park.
Trafalgar Square, Buckingham Palace, the West End theatres and Bond Street are close to the hotel.
The Ritz Restaurant sits beneath a soaring glass roof, and its Executive Chef is John Williams MBE.
The Ritz Restaurant was named Restaurant of the Year at the National Restaurant Awards 2025.
Every Friday and Saturday, Live at The Ritz pairs dinner in The Ritz Restaurant with live music and dancing.
Afternoon Tea includes freshly baked scones with Cornish clotted cream and strawberry preserve, and service is continuous, with courses replenished throughout the visit.
Afternoon Tea is accompanied by a musical ensemble in the 18th-century William Kent House.
The Secret Garden is an outdoor dining and drinking space within the hotel, planted with irises, hellebores, hydrangeas, crab-apple trees and white wisteria.
Grand Deluxe Rooms have marble bathrooms with a deep soaking bathtub, rainfall shower, double vanity and heated marble floors.
The Royal Suite spans two floors, with views of Green Park and The Secret Garden through floor-to-ceiling windows.
The kidz@theritz package provides game consoles for older children, age-appropriate books and DVDs, and a complimentary Ritz teddy for younger children.

highlights.text: The Rivoli Bar has a red and green marble chequerboard floor inspired by William Kent, under restored vaulted ceilings with hand-painted gold motifs.
The hotel's Tea Master, Giandomenico Scanu, travels to tea plantations worldwide to source its loose-leaf teas.
The hotel's 8th-generation Rolls-Royce Phantom EWB was hand-built in England and custom-made to match the hotel's design, and resident guests can hire it.
The Secret Garden was created by Marcus Barnett Studios, with cashmere throws by Johnston's of Elgin as the evening cools.
Afternoon Tea ends with seasonal cakes served tableside from the gueridon trolley.

considerations.text: Gentlemen must wear a jacket and tie for Afternoon Tea and for lunch and dinner in The Ritz Restaurant; smart casual is fine at breakfast, The Rivoli Bar, The Secret Garden and The Cigar Shop, and sportswear is not permitted in any restaurant or bar.
An extra entertainment charge applies to the a la carte and Epicurean menus when live entertainment runs on Friday and Saturday evenings.
The Secret Garden opens weather permitting.
